description: Bohrium is a synthetic chemical element with symbol Bh and atomic number 107, named after Danish physicist Niels Bohr. As a synthetic element, it can only be created in particle accelerators and is not found in nature. In the periodic table, it is a transactinide element in the d-block, a member of the 7th period and group 7 elements as the fifth member of the 6d series of transition metals.
characteristics: All known isotopes of bohrium are highly radioactive; the most stable known isotope is 270Bh with a half-life of approximately 2.4 minutes. Chemistry experiments have confirmed that bohrium behaves as the heavier homologue to rhenium in group 7, with chemical properties that compare well with other group 7 elements. Bohrium is expected to be a solid under normal conditions with a hexagonal close-packed crystal structure and a predicted density of 26–27 g/cm³.
